plots.title: Neo's Awakening
plots.goal: To discover what is wrong with reality and become what he truly is — the One who can reshape the Matrix and free humanity
plots.stakes: Neo's life, the lives of everyone who sacrificed for his belief, and humanity's chance at freedom from machine enslavement

st1.intent: Neo, a hacker who senses something wrong with the world, receives a computer message — 'Follow the white rabbit' — and at a nightclub Trinity tells him the answer he is looking for is looking for him.

st2.intent: Agent Smith captures Neo, seals his mouth shut and inserts a living tracking bug into his navel; Neo refuses to cooperate with the Agents' offer.

st3.intent: Morpheus offers the red pill or the blue pill; Neo takes the red pill, choosing truth over forgetfulness — there is no going back.

st4.intent: Neo wakes naked and bald in a pod among endless towers of human crops; a machine unplugs him and the Nebuchadnezzar retrieves him from the waste system.

st5.intent: Morpheus explains the Matrix and the scorched real world; Neo rejects it violently, demanding to be let out, vomiting and blacking out.

st6.intent: Combat skills are uploaded into Neo's brain; in the dojo he fights Morpheus and learns that Matrix rules can be bent or broken; he fails the jump program and is told death in the Matrix kills the physical body.

st7.intent: The Oracle tells Neo he is not the One but warns that Morpheus will sacrifice his life for Neo's and that one of them will die; Neo leaves believing he is just another guy.

st8.intent: Cypher's betrayal springs at the Hotel Lafayette; the hardline is cut, Mouse is killed, and Morpheus is captured while telling Trinity to get Neo out.

st9.intent: Neo refuses to let Morpheus die and decides to re-enter the Matrix against orders to rescue him; Trinity insists on joining, unable to say what the Oracle told her.

st10.intent: Neo and Trinity storm the government building, massacre the lobby, and fly a helicopter to the executive floor; Neo rakes the office with gunfire and catches Morpheus in a midair cable rescue; he begins to move with superhuman speed.

st11.intent: At the subway station, Agent Smith ambushes Neo; Neo refuses to run, fights hand to hand, and throws Smith in front of a train — declaring his own name rather than Anderson.

st12.intent: Agent Smith pursues Neo through the city and waits in room 303 of the Heart O' the City Hotel; he shoots Neo dead in the chest.

st13.intent: Trinity whispers that the Oracle told her she would fall in love with the One, and that man is Neo; she kisses him and his heart restarts.

st14.intent: Neo awakens as the One — stops the Agents' bullets in midair, sees the Matrix as cascading green code, dives into and destroys Agent Smith from within; the remaining Agents flee.

st15.intent: Morpheus detonates the EMP saving the ship; Neo makes a phone call to the Matrix promising a world without rules and rises into the sky, flying faster than a speeding bullet.

plots.thematic_function: Self-belief earned through sacrifice and love, not bestowed by prophecy: the One is made real by choosing to act on belief without certainty, and by being loved into transformation.

interference.kind: competes_for_belief: Morpheus's conviction that Neo is the One presses against Neo's refusal to accept a destiny he cannot prove
competes_for_survival: Smith's pursuit creates the crucible in which Neo must either die or transform
competes_for_safety: Cypher's betrayal destroys the security Neo has just found and forces the choice that defines the climax

plots.title: Morpheus's Faith
plots.goal: To find, free, and prepare the One — the prophesied savior who will end the machine war and free humanity
plots.stakes: Morpheus's life, his crew's lives, and the five who already died for his belief; if he is wrong again, the search was futile and the dead died for nothing

st1.intent: Morpheus has spent most of his life searching the Matrix for the One; the Oracle prophesied the return of a man who could reshape the Matrix at will.

st2.intent: Morpheus frees Neo, breaking the rule against freeing a mind once it reaches [...]; he believes the search is over.

st3.intent: Morpheus confesses to Neo that five before him died because he misunderstood the Oracle — he believed it was about him, not about the ones he chose; his belief is personal and fallible, not procedural.

st4.intent: Morpheus takes Neo to see the Oracle and confesses his unshakeable belief that Neo is the One; he asks Neo to trust him.

st5.intent: When the betrayal springs, Morpheus fights Agent Smith hand to hand and tells Trinity to get Neo out — 'He is all that matters' — sacrificing himself to protect Neo.

st6.intent: Morpheus is captured and tortured by Agent Smith, who injects a serum to hack his mind and extract the access codes to Zion's mainframe.

st7.intent: Neo and Trinity storm the building and rescue Morpheus; he breaks his own restraints and is pulled to safety — his faith in Neo vindicated when Neo becomes the One.

plots.thematic_function: Belief as a personal, fallible, and costly act: Morpheus's faith is not procedural certainty but a wager of lives on a feeling — and the story vindicates not the prophecy but the man who staked everything on it.

interference.kind: competes_for_agent: Morpheus's certainty presses Neo toward a destiny Neo resists; the mentor's belief becomes the student's burden
competes_for_crew: Cypher's resentment of Morpheus's belief is the direct counter-argument — 'He lied to us, he tricked us'
competes_for_morpheus_body: Smith wants the codes in Morpheus's mind; Morpheus would rather die than give them

plots.title: Trinity's Love
plots.goal: To love Neo and, when the moment comes, tell him the Oracle's prophecy so that her love can revive him as the One
plots.stakes: If she does not confess, Neo stays dead and the prophecy fails — the One is lost with him

st1.intent: In the opening phone call, Cypher asks Trinity 'You like him, don't you?' and presses whether she believes Neo is the One; Trinity deflects, but the Oracle's prophecy that she would fall in love with the One is already in motion.

st2.intent: Cypher notices Trinity watching Neo with unusual attention and asks 'There's something about him, isn't there?'; Trinity does not answer.

st3.intent: Trinity brings Neo dinner while he sleeps and breathes in his scent; Cypher catches her and implies she has feelings, but she deflects again.

st4.intent: In the car on the way to the Oracle, Trinity tries to tell Neo what the Oracle told her but is physically unable to speak — the words stop in her throat.

st5.intent: At the subway station, Trinity begins to tell Neo what the Oracle said — 'she told me I was going to fall [...] a train blasts into the station, drowning her voice; Neo asks her to promise to tell him the rest.

st6.intent: Neo is shot dead; Trinity whispers that the Oracle said she would love the One, that Neo is that man, and that she loves him; she kisses him and his heart restarts.

st7.intent: Neo revives — the prophecy is fulfilled not by the Oracle's declaration but by Trinity's act of love, which is what makes the One real.

plots.thematic_function: Love as the resurrection trigger: the Oracle's prophecy is self-fulfilling, not declarative — it is Trinity's confession, not the Oracle's words, that makes Neo the One. The One is made real by being loved.

interference.kind: competes_for_clock: Trinity's unspoken truth must wait until death to be spoken; the delay creates the dramatic structure of the resurrection
competes_for_trinity: Cypher's 'I thought I was in [...]' probes Trinity's feelings and exposes her vulnerability

plots.title: Cypher's Betrayal
plots.goal: To escape the real world by betraying Morpheus to Agent Smith in exchange for reinsertion into the Matrix as a rich man with no memory
plots.stakes: Morpheus's life, the crew's lives, Zion's security codes, and the life of Neo — whom Cypher nearly unplugs

st1.intent: Cypher confides to Neo over drinks that he regrets taking the red pill — 'Why, oh why, didn't I [...]?' — revealing his desire to return to ignorance.

st2.intent: Cypher tells Neo that five before him died because Morpheus got them amped up believing in bullshit; he advises Neo to run from Agents — 'Run your ass off.'

st3.intent: Cypher secretly meets Agent Smith in a restaurant and agrees to betray Morpheus in exchange for reinsertion into the Matrix as a rich, important man with no memory of the real world.

st4.intent: After entering the Matrix with the crew, Cypher drops a cellular phone into a garbage can, signaling the Agents and enabling the trap at the Hotel Lafayette.

st5.intent: The hardline is cut, the windows are bricked up, Mouse is gunned down, and Morpheus is captured while fighting Agent Smith to let Trinity and Neo escape.

st6.intent: Cypher exits the Matrix first, shoots Tank and Dozer with a lightning rifle, and unplugs Apoc and Switch, killing them instantly; he prepares to unplug Neo.

st7.intent: Tank — wounded but alive — levels the gun and fires a crackling bolt that kills Cypher before he can unplug Neo; Cypher dies in disbelief.

plots.thematic_function: The anti-Neo: someone who took the red pill and regretted it. Cypher's 'why didn't I take the blue pill' is the counter-argument to the premise — ignorance is bliss — and his betrayal tests the cost of belief by destroying those who paid for it.

interference.kind: competes_for_neo_life: Cypher nearly unplugs Neo, the would-be One, from his chair — the survival of the protagonist hangs on Tank's survival
competes_for_morpheus: Cypher delivers Morpheus to Smith, converting the mentor's sacrifice into the antagonist's victory
enables_antagonist: Cypher's signal to the Agents is what makes the capture of Morpheus possible

plots.title: Agent Smith's Hunt
plots.goal: To capture Morpheus, extract Zion's access codes, destroy the human resistance, and — beneath it all — to escape the Matrix he despises
plots.stakes: Zion's destruction and humanity's permanent enslavement; for Smith personally, continued imprisonment in a reality he cannot stand

st1.intent: Agents confirm their next target is a hacker named Neo; they pursue Trinity through the opening chase but she escapes through a ringing phone.

st2.intent: Smith captures Neo, details his double life, and offers a deal — cooperate or lose everything; when Neo refuses, Smith seals his mouth and inserts a tracking bug.

st3.intent: Alerted by Cypher's signal, the Agents and police flood the Hotel Lafayette; the hardline is cut and the crew is trapped.

st4.intent: Smith tortures Morpheus with a serum to extract Zion's codes and reveals his true motive — he hates the Matrix, calls it a zoo, a prison, and wants to escape; 'I must get out of [...].'

st5.intent: Smith ambushes Neo at the subway station; Neo refuses to run and fights hand to hand, throwing Smith in front of a train, but Smith reconstitutes and pursues.

st6.intent: Smith waits in room 303 of the Heart O' the City Hotel and shoots Neo dead in the chest; he stands over the body and says goodbye.

st7.intent: Neo, revived as the One, dives into and destroys Agent Smith from within; the remaining Agents flee in fear for the first time since their inception.

plots.thematic_function: The antagonist as mirror: Smith wants to escape the Matrix as much as any freed human, but his method is control and destruction. His rage against the 'zoo, this prison' gives him a sympathisable motive — from his perspective, humans are the virus and he is the cure.

interference.kind: competes_for_neo_life: Smith's pursuit creates the crucible in which Neo must either die or transcend
competes_for_morpheus_mind: Smith wants the codes in Morpheus's mind; the crew would rather kill Morpheus than let him break
enabled_by_betrayal: Cypher's deal with Smith is what makes the capture of Morpheus possible — the antagonist's success depends on the traitor's access
